name: AD846
tagline: Obsolete ADI 450 V/µs current-feedback amp with 0.01% settling, still prized by DIYers for DAC I/V stages.

lineage.note: Sole source; sibling of AD844/AD811. SPICE macro-model Rev. A dated 1/91. Now obsolete.

part_numbers.note: Family base number; ADI lists it under obsolete products.
N-8 plastic DIP, −40 to +85 °C; B grade 75 µV max Vos.
Q-8 cerdip, −55 to +125 °C; /883B is MIL-STD-883B processed, NSN-listed.

key_specs.condition: typ; settling: 10 V step, G −1 to −10

reputation.summary: A small diyAudio niche calls it 'great sounding' for DAC I/V conversion; one thread asks if there is a better-sounding op-amp, and another hunts for a replacement since it went obsolete. ADI's own AD1862 DAC datasheet names the NE5534 or AD846 for the I/V stage. The praise is niche, not wide consensus.
typical_uses: DAC current-to-voltage (I/V) stage, e.g. after the AD1862
Output and line stages in DIY DACs and CD-player mods
caveats: Obsolete: any stock sold today is old or of unknown origin.
Current feedback: the feedback resistor sets bandwidth and stability, so voltage-feedback parts may not drop in.
A diyAudio poster notes it was 'only 12 bit accurate' (0.01%) and saw little commercial success.

counterfeit_notes: No documented counterfeits. Long obsolete, so treat 'new' AN/BN/AQ/BQ marketplace stock as suspect (possibly remarked AD844/AD811 or pulls). Check quiescent current (6.5 mA max) and that bandwidth tracks the feedback resistor.
alternatives: NE5534 (voltage feedback; named in AD1862 datasheet)
